title: Prefix and Aspect 1: A Prefix Makes a Verb Perfective
titleRussian: Приставка и вид 1: Приставка делает глагол совершенным
description: A simplex imperfective verb plus a prefix usually becomes perfective. With a pure perfectivizing prefix the meaning stays the same; only the aspect changes. писать → написать, читать → прочитать, делать → сделать.
descriptionRussian: Простой глагол несовершенного вида с приставкой обычно становится совершенным. С чисто видовой приставкой значение не меняется — меняется только вид. писать → написать, читать → прочитать, делать → сделать.
intro: This short book is the bridge between the two you just did. Aspect gave you pairs; prefixes gave you meaning shades. Here is how they connect: an unprefixed verb is almost always imperfective, and adding a prefix almost always makes it perfective. Which prefix does that for a given verb is arbitrary and has to be learned one verb at a time.
rules: A simplex verb (a root with no prefix) is almost always imperfective: писать, читать, делать, готовить, учить, строить. It names a process or a habit.
Adding a prefix to a simplex imperfective usually makes it perfective: писать → написать, читать → прочитать, делать → сделать.
With a pure (empty) perfectivizing prefix the meaning does not change, only the aspect. писать and написать both mean 'to write'; написать frames it as a completed result.
Each simplex verb takes its own perfectivizing prefix and you cannot predict it: писать → на-, читать → про-, делать → с-, строить → по-, учить → вы-. Learn the partner with the verb.
The prefixed perfective has a past and a future but no present. For an ongoing present action, use the simplex imperfective: я пишу (now), but я напишу (future).
examples: писать → написать (to write). Я пишу письмо. (process, present) / Я написал письмо. (completed result, past)
читать → прочитать (to read). Она читает книгу. / Она прочитала книгу. The pure prefix про- only seals the action.
делать → сделать (to do). Я делаю задание. / Я сделал задание. Pure prefix с-, same meaning, perfective.
строить → построить (to build). Они строят дом. / Они построили дом. Pure prefix по-.
учить → выучить (to learn by heart). Я учу слова. / Я выучил слова. Pure prefix вы-, completion of the learning.
готовить → приготовить (to cook, prepare). Мама готовит ужин. / Мама приготовила ужин. Pure prefix при-.

tables.title: Simplex imperfective → prefixed perfective (pure perfectivizing prefix)

items.prompt: Вчера я _____ длинное письмо и отправил его.
items.promptEnglish: Yesterday I wrote a long letter and sent it.
items.hint: One completed result, finished and then sent. Which member of писать / написать?
items.explanation: A single completed result ('wrote it, then sent it') needs the perfective. The perfective of писать is built with the pure prefix на-: написать → написал (masc past). Писал is the imperfective process; пишу is the present.

items.prompt: Какая приставка делает глагол читать совершенным?
items.promptEnglish: Which prefix makes the verb читать perfective?
items.hint: Recall the pair from the aspect track: читать / ___читать.
items.explanation: The perfective of читать is прочитать, built with про-. Each simplex verb takes its own perfectivizing prefix and you cannot predict it: писать takes на-, делать takes с-, строить takes по-, but читать takes про-.

items.prompt: Сейчас Антон _____ задание; он закончит через час.
items.promptEnglish: Right now Anton is doing the assignment; he will finish in an hour.
items.hint: An ongoing action happening now. Perfectives have no present tense.
items.explanation: 'Сейчас' marks an action in progress now. A perfective verb has no present tense, so сделал (past) and сделает (future) cannot describe 'right now.' Use the simplex imperfective present: делает.

items.prompt: Завтра я _____ это упражнение и пришлю тебе.
items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow I will do this exercise and send it to you.
items.hint: 'Завтра' plus one completed action that has a result. Future of the perfective.
items.explanation: 'Завтра' plus a single completed result needs the perfective future. The perfective of делать is сделать (pure prefix с-); its future first-person form is сделаю. Делаю would be the imperfective present, which does not fit a future, completed action.

items.prompt: Мама два часа _____ ужин, и наконец он был готов.
items.promptEnglish: Mom cooked dinner for two hours, and at last it was ready.
items.hint: 'Два часа' stresses the duration of the process, not just the end point.
items.explanation: 'Два часа' (for two hours) foregrounds the duration of the process, which calls for the imperfective: готовила. The perfective приготовила would put all the weight on the finished result. Note that the perfective partner of готовить is приготовить (pure prefix при-).

items.prompt: Рабочие наконец _____ новый дом на нашей улице.
items.promptEnglish: The workers finally built a new house on our street.
items.hint: 'Наконец' (finally) points to a completed result. Which prefix gives строить its perfective?
items.explanation: 'Наконец' (finally) signals a completed result, so use the perfective past. The perfective of строить is построить (pure prefix по-): построили. Строили would describe the ongoing building, and строят is the present.

items.prompt: Я _____ письмо и пошла на почту.
items.promptEnglish: I (f) wrote the letter (finished it) and went to the post office.
items.hint: The pure perfectivizing prefix for писать.
items.explanation: Писать takes на- as its pure perfectivizer: написала. Писала is the imperfective process; записала adds the 'note down' meaning, so it is not the pure partner.

items.promptEnglish: She read the book through over the weekend.
items.explanation: Читать takes про-: прочитала. Читала is the process; перечитала adds 'again'; зачитала adds 'aloud / to pieces', so neither is the pure partner.

items.promptEnglish: Anton built the dacha (finished it) in two years.
items.explanation: Строить takes по-: построил. Строил is the process; перестроил means 'rebuilt'; застроил 'built up an area', both adding extra meaning.

items.prompt: Завтра я _____ ужин для всей семьи.
items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow I will cook dinner for the whole family.
items.hint: One completed future result of готовить.
items.explanation: The perfective partner of готовить is приготовить, and its future is synthetic: приготовлю. Буду готовить would promise only the process; готовлю is the present.

blanks: За выходные я _____ всю книгу. (Over the weekend I read the whole book through.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'Всю книгу за выходные' frames a complete, bounded result: one read-through finished over the weekend. That needs the perfective прочитал, built from читать with the pure prefix про-. Читал would be the ongoing process with no completion claim.

errorCorrection.sentence: Не мешай, я сейчас напишу важное письмо.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Don't disturb me, I'm writing an important letter right now.
errorCorrection.explanation: An action in progress right now needs the imperfective present: пишу. The prefixed perfective написать has no present tense, so напишу is the future ('I will write'), not 'I am writing'. Написал is the perfective past; написать the infinitive. For an ongoing present action, fall back to the simplex imperfective (пишу), never the prefixed perfective.

errorCorrection.sentence: Целый год рабочие построили новый мост через реку.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: For a whole year, the workers were building a new bridge over the river.
errorCorrection.explanation: The bare duration 'целый год' (for a whole year) foregrounds the process and takes the imperfective: строили. The perfective построили claims a completed result and does not combine with a bare duration accusative (it would need 'за год' = within a year for the completed reading). Строят (present) and построят (future) clash with the past process. Duration of an activity selects the imperfective, even though the perfective partner is built with the prefix по-.

errorCorrection.sentence: За один вечер Антон учил все новые слова к тесту.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In one evening, Anton learned all the new words for the test.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'За один вечер' (within one evening) plus 'все слова' frames a completed, bounded result, which needs the perfective: выучил. The imperfective учил describes the ongoing process of studying and does not combine with the 'за + accusative' completion frame. Учит is the present; выучит the future. The perfective partner of учить is выучить, built with the prefix вы-.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Right now I am writing a letter, wait a minute.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Сейчас' plus an action in progress needs the imperfective present. The simplex imperfective писать gives пишу. The prefixed perfective напишу is a future ('I will write'), because perfectives have no present tense.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ это письмо за пять минут и отдам тебе.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I will write this letter in five minutes and give it to you.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'За пять минут' plus a completed result points to the perfective. The perfective of писать is написать (pure prefix на-), future напишу. The imperfective пишу could not express a single bounded, completed future action.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each verb by aspect: simplex imperfective (no prefix) or prefixed perfective.

reviewVocab.definition: simplex verb (a bare root with no prefix; almost always imperfective, e.g., писать, читать, делать)
reviewVocab.example: Глагол писать — простой и несовершенного вида; с приставкой на- он становится совершенным: написать.

reviewVocab.definition: aspect pair (the imperfective and perfective forms of the same action; the perfective is usually the prefixed member)
reviewVocab.example: писать / написать — это видовая пара: несовершенный и совершенный вид одного действия.

reviewVocab.definition: pure (empty) perfectivizing prefix: a prefix that adds only the perfective aspect, no new meaning (на- in написать, с- in сделать)
reviewVocab.example: В паре делать / сделать приставка с- чисто видовая: значение то же, меняется только вид.
